headline: Two tankers + tugboat caught fire overnight on 'unauthorized' Hormuz routes, two 'Lucas' drones seized

sections.what_happened: In a Thursday-morning statement marking '250 days of steadfastness', the IRGC said that overnight, in two separate incidents, a large oil tanker attempting to cross the unauthorized southern route of the Strait of Hormuz struck a mine, caught fire and was stopped; a second supertanker leaving the same route east of the strait was stopped in a large fire, and a tugboat that approached it to help extinguish the blaze also caught fire. The statement added that IRGC Navy electronic-warfare units took control of two intruding 'Lucas' drones, guiding them to land safely and seizing them as spoils, and warned that US insistence on vessels violating the rules imposes heavy insurance costs on American taxpayers and regional allies. The IRGC named no vessels, flags, positions or crew status.
sections.what_verified: Statement relay confirmed by 6 distinct publisher families (see corroboration_families). Mehr News Agency carried the full statement but has NO declared tier in the source registry, so it is reported with attribution and does NOT count toward corroboration. Event corroboration is nil: every family derives from the single IRGC statement, so repetition does not raise the verification label for the incidents themselves.
sections.what_disputed: (1) NUMBER DISCREPANCY ACROSS THREE DAYS: Nov 3 IRGC claim = 3 tankers hit mines (recorded Nov 3); Nov 4 claim = 4 tankers destroyed + 2 vessels detained + 56th MQ-9 downed (recorded Nov 4 0900-02/1600-02); Nov 5 claim = 2 tankers + 1 tugboat + 2 drones seized. No reconciliation offered. (2) CENTCOM disputed the Nov 4 claim (per crisis.zone Nov 4 monitor; prior scan records CENTCOM's position that the strait is cleared of mines and flows had returned to prewar levels). (3) No UKMTO advisory matching either the Nov 4 or Nov 5 mine claims had surfaced as of the Nov 4 monitors; the only UKMTO-confirmed Hormuz-area incident remains the separate Nov 3 projectile strike on a tanker ~14 nm northeast of Lima, Oman (projectiles, not mines). (4) Market shrug: Brent fell below $100/bbl on Nov 4 (recorded Nov 4 2100-02). (5) Khaama/Reuters note the Nov 5 claims 'had not been independently verified, and no immediate confirmation from maritime authorities or the vessels operators was reported.'
sections.why_matters: Claim-bust, moment-first: IRGC's third tanker count in three days — 3, then 4, now 2 + a tug. The statement is real; the fires are not yet proven. Lead with the discrepancy and the missing hull names, not the fire.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP + IN-WINDOW RELAY (Reuters 04:21Z = 08:21 ; Mehr 04:25Z = 08:25 ; Moneycontrol relay 10:34 IST = 09:04 , in-window) — IRGC Nov 5 morning statement: two tankers + tugboat caught fire overnight on 'unauthorized' Hormuz routes, two 'Lucas' drones seized; vessel count differs from the Nov 4 four-tanker claim

totw_analysis: Our read: Claim-bust, moment-first: IRGC's third tanker count in three days — 3, then 4, now 2 + a tug. The statement is real; the fires are not yet proven. Lead with the discrepancy and the missing hull names, not the fire. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Proof vs claim: is Iran actually enforcing a mined blockade in Hormuz, or inflating unverifiable tanker claims to raise insurance costs and force talks — and should a third different count in three days be reported as enforcement at all?
